statement.p: A tank in the shape of an inverted right circular cone has height 6 meters and radius 2 meters. It is filled with 5 meters of hot chocolate. Find the work required to empty the tank by pumping the hot chocolate over the top of the tank. The density of hot chocolate is \delta = 1030 \ \textrm{kg}/\textrm{m}^3. Your answer must include the correct .

solution.p: We think of the tank as made from infinitely many 'infinitesimal' horizontal slices, with x the vertical distance an infinitesimal slice of the water is from the bottom of the tank (the vertex of the right circular cone).
A cross section through the vertical center to the side is approximated below (not necessarily to scale).

Now the large right triangle with height 6 and top side length 2 is similar to the right triangle with height x and top side length r. So \frac{6}{2} = \frac{x}{r}\implies 6 r = 2 x or r = {\frac{1}{3}} x.
Therefore the area of every infinitesimal slice is A(x) = \pi(r)^2=\pi({\frac{1}{3}} x)^2={\frac{1}{9}} \pi x^2 \text{meter}^2.

The infinitesimal slice has volume dV=A(x)dx = {\frac{1}{9}} \pi x^2\,dx \text{meter}^3, and since mass = density\times volume, the mass of our infinitesimal slice is dm = \delta dV where \delta= 1030 \frac{kg}{\text{meter}^3}.
So the mass of the slice at x is \delta\,dV= (1030)\left({\frac{1}{9}} \pi x^2\right)\,dx kg. We now must find mgh for each slice.
Each slice at x must be lifted a height h = (6-x) meters, and g=9.8 \frac{meters}{sec^2} . So mgh for each slice is 9.8(1030)\left({\frac{1}{9}} \pi x^2\right)(6-x)\,dx Joules.
